## Summary
When a synthesis contradicts its primary sources, trust the primary sources. Systematic reviews compress information; compression loses detail that sometimes reverses the conclusion.

## Why it works
Synthesis introduces two layers of error: sampling bias in study selection and aggregation error in effect-size combination. Primary data carries neither of these artefacts by construction.

## Transferable pattern
- Cite primary studies, not meta-analyses, when a claim is contested.
- When a meta-analysis conflicts with a landmark primary study, read the primary study.
- Record confidence lower when your only source is a secondary synthesis.

## Use when
- Evaluating evidentiary strength of a claim for corpus promotion.
- Deciding authority tier for a new source (primary vs secondary vs rumour).
- Writing confidence scores on entries derived from secondary sources.

## Avoid when
- The domain has no accessible primary literature (policy documents, grey literature).
- Speed matters more than precision and a trusted synthesis is available.
